status: Historically supported completion; cipher-only alternatives remain 5/6
new_application: The French telegram and German calendar were already reviewed for p176b. This certificate applies that existing historical evidence to newly source-edited p166/p167/p170 B reports and their different November 7–9 square; it makes no first-discovery claim for the historical sources or p176b plaintext.
basis: The historical identity of the reserve division supplies VF=6; the remaining unused digit supplies XA=5 under the bijective square convention. Neither assignment is made in data/keys.json.

sources.source_type: Contemporary operational telegram, reproduced in a later scholarly source edition
sources.publication_title: Documents diplomatiques français sur l’histoire du Bassin des Carpates, 1918–1932
sources.sender: General Franchet d’Esperey, Commander in Chief of the Allied Armies of the Orient
sources.observation: The report explicitly includes the 6th Reserve Division with the reconstituted German 11th Army; the same paragraph lists the Alpenkorps and the 217th and 219th divisions in the Nagy-Backskerek–Verschatz area. The matching units and geography support reading 6 in the earlier German reports. This is historical corroboration, not an independent decipherment of the received coordinates.

limitations: The primary telegram describes the situation on 11 November and was transmitted on 19 November; the German intercepts are dated 9 November.
The two-digit ambiguity is not resolved by ciphertext arithmetic alone.
The source-derived prefix and all pre-existing editorial corrections remain separately documented. Selecting the historical digit adds no ciphertext substitutions.
The historical context supports the reserve-division identification; it does not certify every other occurrence of an unknown cell in a corrupted intercept.
The later-key p176b message requires its own source and key analysis; the November7–9 mapping does not automatically transfer.
